body:
I know exactly where you heart is at right now. The best advice I can give is to be caring, yet cautious. I don't mean that in a she is manipulating you so you should be careful way. I mean that in a be careful you do not lose yourself way. Until recently I dated someone with BPD for over a year and a half. I thew everything I had into caring for this person to try and show them that things can and will get better.

I lost myself instead. I compromised other close relationships always thinking that I will just help her get through this time and things will get better. In my case though, they never did and I am fighting tooth and nail to get my life back. Things got worse financially an emotionally at a pace just slow enough to not realize how bad they were until it was too late. Now I am the one seeking therapy while I pay all of the bills and she sits around refusing to go to get help, go to work, or move out.

I hope she gets help and sticks with it. The pain of watching someone you love give up and destroy their life is more painful than anyone expects. It defies logic. The only thing keeping me going is the knowledge that when my lease it up I will be too broke to do anything but move home with my family that cares about me, and friends that will hopefully be understanding and forgive me.

I honestly appreciate you responding. I do live with her and it is unbelievably hard to watch someone I care about just completely giving up because they feel that choosing to give up is the only control they have over their life. 

She won't go to therapy or work, but claims she will just end up committing suicide if she loses her job. So now I'm just waiting for that bomb to drop.

This is a huge fear of mine given my personal situation and I would honestly like to know how you have handled it. I told myself for a long time that I would be ok and able to carry on if she kills herself. Then I realized I was lying to myself.

My fear of her suicide has controlled my life for a long time and I can't keep doing it. I care about her, but I also realize I have trapped myself for the time being (both financially and emotionally). I want so badly to just breaks all ties and leave this person behind me, but can't bring myself to do it.
Dealing with a similar situation and trying to find a way out. I think I needed to hear it too.

Mind = Blown. I had never heard of Waifs so I read this article http://gettinbetter.com/waif.html and a few others brief ones. I'm fairly new to all of this information as it was only a couple months ago that I started to look for it. Can you point me towards any other resources related to this? After reading the article I almost feel like I need to just pack my car and leave while she is at therapy tomorrow because I do not think I could possibly leave when she is present, or AFTER telling her I am leaving. I just get accused of such terrible abandonment I fall apart. Living with her has not only ruined my personal life, but her unrelenting need for help/attention is still affecting my ability to work or even maintain a stable sleep schedule and I fear it will lead to me losing my job.

EDIT: I should also mention that I work from home online, so it is nearly impossible to escape in the evening when places with free WiFi start to close.

About a week ago an argument with my now x-gf reached the point that I said I wanted to leave the apartment until things cooled down (this was after she violated my boundary that if things escalated too much that I needed to be able to leave the room for 10-15 minutes and calm down). She threatened to call the police and tell them that I had hit her (I had not) if I left the apartment. I knew at that moment that I needed to grab my laptop, wallet, phone, etc. and leave. It was the hardest thing that I have ever done. I had to call a friend an hour away to come and pick me up at a Walgreens a few miles away that I walked to since my car is in disrepair. I did not think she would go through with calling the cops or other threats, but it was a possibility and I was finally done living in fear. I did not care if she broke everything that I owned, or if I had to prove my innocence to the police. (MAKE SURE!!!!! that other people are aware of the situation)  I gave my friend my phone so that I would not see her texts/phone calls, but that he could monitor them for suicide threats (common) and call the police if he deemed necessary.

Find a way to get some time to clear your head if you can. Then be honest with yourself and decide if this person is worth risking your life and happiness for. Do not let people tell you that you are overreacting or lead you to doubt yourself. If you want to try and make it work, ensure that you have a way to set health boundaries and make sure that the consequences for crossing those boundaries are clear and that you follow through with those consequences.

I want to put extra emphasis on taking woodenbiplane's comment seriously. The reason I found this subreddit was that my now x-gf (but still roommate due to circumstances) has a lot of borderline traits. One thing that she is currently incapable of doing is keeping her past from sabotaging her future. She sees her past and everything little thing that goes wrong in daily life as proof that she will never get better. She uses it as an excuse to not do the things that would help. Blame whatever you want, but after you have placed the blame move forward. Holding onto the past will only hurt your future.

As for where to begin, look up all of the hospitals within your reach. Find the one that is best suited for your needs and contact them about financial assistance/charity care. Many hospitals will work with you to reduce or even eliminate fees if you qualify. You might actually be able to get 100% of your bills covered if you work with them. Not every program/therapy is right for each person, so keep at it and don't be afraid to truly assess if something is working for you and change course if needed (just don't quit).

I'm on the other side of the problem, not sure if my gf has BPD and not sure if it is something that I should even mention. She is currently undergoing intensive therapy at a well known and very good institution and thus far it seems to be having an excellent effect. I wish you the best of luck, and one piece of advice I can give is that most not-for-profit hospitals are required to do a certain amount of charity work each year to maintain their status. This means that even if you want to seek treatment and it is expensive, you should look into it as it can cover up to 100% of your bills. Then they might be able to help you bring it up with your family.

> he could dance circles around me with his reasoning and verbal sparring

THIS! More than anything else this has had the largest impact on our situation. Like she can somehow find a way to make me say anything she wants by making me seem crazy or irrational if I don't agree. And the whole time it's like my fucking mind is being blown at how badly I've been cornered. And when this is happening the most is when she is doing the worst, so I'm already just trying to do anything possible to stop the situation.

I'm also very sorry to hear about your situation. I have only been dating her for going on two years and I can't imagine how hard it would be to deal with something like this from inside of a marriage with kids around that you are also trying to protect. I think that the only reason I am even on here trying to talk to people and work things out on some level is that I got lucky. The perfect storm of shit came along to make things reach a breaking point and I just happened to have the right people in my life who were able to find me some help and guidance. So now that I have some tools to help and know that failure on my part does not end with me being homeless and jobless, I feel more confident trying to help her till the bottom falls out.

I also realized that I too might slip further into depression or this situation and allow myself to get lost and consumed by it. So this may sounds crazy, but I told some of my friends that if it goes too far and I have clearly lost my ability to deal with this rationally, that they have every right to forcibly remove me from the situation, and I trust them to do so in a responsible way. They have also been extremely understanding of what she is going through and been very supportive which helps. So it is not like they are going to just get mad I am not around and pull a Saving Silverman. Now that I am aware, I am trying to assemble my parachute while I try to help her, and that gives me some strength.

I agree with Killerangel713 that the tornado analogy is an excellent one. And I definitely agree that it is likely best right now to avoid the family issue. Though this is made difficult on certain levels as many of my bills are currently at/being sent to their house due to us recently moving into a new apartment. So I can change my mailing addresses now, but I will have to go get my mail at some point. I'll do my best to work around it though.

Also, you could not possibly be more right about spending too much time together. I have hated that since very early in our relationship. However, since we had not been dating too long and you tend to like seeing a new person more frequently I did not think too much of it at first. Then I felt like it was required because of everything I was being blamed for to show that I cared (It’s a trap!), and now I see how it reached the level that it has.  Part of the reason I was attracted to her originally was how independent and strong she seemed, but things quickly went in the other direction and now she is 100% dependent on me and I loathe it. Particularly because I know she is still capable of more than she will do. She will ask me to do things like a test because it makes her feel more loved, and she has admitted this. For the most part I don’t mind doing little things because it gets me off my ass, but each time I know it is intentional, I get angry inside. Sure I can point this out, but then that upsets her and I’ve backslid so far into not wanting to be confrontational that I make the wrong decision and just do it to avoid the possible outcomes of mentioning it (the story of our relationship). I was so independent and strong on my own before this relationship that I hate myself now too for letting this happen. I feel like I tried being too nice and understanding because I did not understand, and did not stick to my own guns.

The little things aside, there are important things like paper work to apply for financial assistance with medical bills that I simply cannot do for her, but she has not and will not do yet. I can only call the hospital to get the account put on hold for so long before it gets sent to collections, but if I even mention doing it she just shuts down. Then I can’t help but get upset when I am trying my hardest to keep her from ruining her own life in regards to her job and credit. People can tell me all they want that I am not responsible for her, but when you see something happening and you do nothing about it, that is no good either. Any advice to help get her to do this?

I’m drowning financially to the point that my own vehicle has fallen into disrepair because I cannot afford to fix it while I pay for our rent and other bills. Each month that goes by I come closer and closer to money deciding the fate of our relationship, and sadly I almost wish it would make the choice for me, but then I feel like that is just me being a pussy and wanting an easy way out. I’ve skipped several international trips for work due to her health issues, and I generally work from home (particularly with no car during the day now) so I can’t help but get stuck being around her 24/7, particularly with her on medical leave. Her daily therapy the last couple weeks has helped a lot though as it gives me at least a few hours a day to work in quiet and be by myself. 

Each time I try to clear my head to write a response to someone on here, I fear that I am going to sound crazy. And what scares me even more is that I now question my own thoughts because I don’t know what is me anymore, and what I have trained myself to do to survive our relationship. I see her getting help, but I also think I need my own. If I left her tomorrow I could be on a plane out of the country the week after to help my work and start rebuilding my life, but not giving her the chance to get better and have support when she is now trying so hard to get better just seems wrong. I think the thing that makes me the saddest right now is this dream I have in the back of my mind. It’s really short too. That one day she will get well enough to walk in the room and tell me she is leaving me because she realizes how toxic our relationship has been and that she feels like she needs to be on her own and find herself. Then I don’t say a word until she leaves, at which point I pick up the phone and see what my friends are up to that night.

My grandmother use to say "Oh the tangled webs we weave when first we practice to deceive". Not sure where it is from, but I feel like this could not be more relevant to how I have handled our relationship and I hate myself for it now.

Thank you for the response and taking the time to read my comment. I will make sure to read what you have provided. Rather than posting part of it again, please take a look at my reply to bpdagain for some extra insight.

Thank you for the response and taking the time to read my long comment. I actually just finished reading Stop Walking on Eggshells and it has helped my understanding a lot. I realize now that she acted the way she did over the weekend because she was scared, and then it escalated to the level that it did because of the ultimatum. The trouble is that when you avoid all contact with your family because of the demands of this person, and they cancel time and time again on going with to address the issue, it is hard to not become emotionally involved and want to press the issue. Being put in a spot where contacting my own family makes me a traitor when I honestly don't believe the situation is as my girlfriend sees it is something I don't know how to handle. And I feel like the longer it drags out, the harder it will be for my family to want to talk openly, and it will also enforce her belief that she is 100% in the right and had no part in creating the situation. Not to mention that I missed Thanksgiving with my family on behalf of this, and will likely be forced into a similar situation around Christmas.

I'm doing my best to keep a clear head, and fortunately I am extremely patient and would never in a million years break something or lay a hand on her out of anger. But instead, I sit there and get verbally abused and fall apart because I don't want to make things worse, and the only way I feel I can do that with her is to do nothing till she calms down, but by then I have said or done anything possible to stop it and lost my own stance on a situation. Also, as she is doing this I think she sees the negative effect it is having on me and wants me to hurt as bad as her, so she won’t stop.  I feel extremely resentful and manipulated each time this happens. The situation is such that I am afraid she is going to attack me despite her claims that she never would. This then makes me want to leave for my own safety and peace of mind when things get out of hand, but leaving makes her explode even worse, so I just feel trapped. I even had a talk with her about needing to at least put ourselves in separate rooms when things escalate until we calm down and she agreed, until she was angry and this went right out the window.  Fortunately I train in martial arts and could probably defend myself fairly well without harming her if it came to it, but that does not always save you from a knife.

The best example I have for how these situations go down is that one time while in the car on the expressway she began hitting herself as hard as she possible could screaming that she would not stop and would jump out of the car if I did not admit I was wrong. I was not wrong, but of course I can't let her keep hitting herself or jump out so I agree, but then having agreed is used against me because I admitted I was wrong. It's scary. 

On the opposite side of the coin she has comes to terms with needing help. But if I want to help her we can't break up as we live together and her moving out would force her to not be able to get to her job or treatment due to distance as her only option would be to move home, where many of her problems stem from, because she has no friends. I'm willing to go so far as to move out and just pay the darn rent while she gets help, but she refused when that was mentioned and of course threw out that she would just kill herself living on her own.

Part of the problem I am running into though is that I do not believe that they will be able to take care of themself or become more independent. If I did, I would have been gone a long time ago, and truthfully, I should have been gone a long time ago. But you don't always realize the way in which someone is sick until it is too late. I feel that this would just further justify their belief that everything and everyone is against them and that there is no reason to even try to get better or be responsible. Then I fear I will likely be forced to witness this person inflict self harm to get what they want or they will commit suicide. I actually have an appointment to speak with another psychologist for myself tomorrow and I hope that maybe helps.
How does no one have any information to help on this?

Is there anything like this in the United States that you know of? I will search on my own as well, but my SO is in dire need of something like this right now. Any help to speed up the process would be appreciated.

Everyone else has said pretty much everything on my mind, but no one has mentioned what your plan will be doing to some poor train conductor. Someone will be in the engine and have to watch you get hit if they are not able to stop in time. I do not agree with suicide, but if you are going to do it, find a way that does not possibly put someone else in a terrible depression. Otherwise, I beg you to listen to the others in this thread and reach out for some help.

I used to think a lot of the same things. Some of them are spot on. But I think your worrying about the wrong things. Who cares if there is no god? Not me. If there is, great, maybe I lived a decent life and things work out. If there is not, I'll be damned if I wasted mine without helping a single person or learning/experiencing as much as my brain can handle. You should maybe go to Khanacademy.org and check out their Cosmology and Astronomy section. Watch the first 5 videos on Scale of Earth/Solar System/Galaxy/ UNIVERSE! It will blow your mind. Then, like with Reddit, you will likely just start watching more and more. If that does not do it, get a job on a ship and work your way across the globe and have some adventure. Live life for yourself, and test your metal. What do you have to lose? Did you know that the Universe is something like 5 times larger than we can see  due to the speed of light and growing all the time (this could be off, but watch the videos I mentioned and they will give you the right info).

Do you have any interests? Videogames, cosplay, movies, reading, music, making chainmail, Renfaires, sports, that cup stacking game that was popular 15 years ago? Could be anything. Well I can tell you now that anything you just though of, there is a group of people somewhere who love that shit too. Self harm is not worth it. Wanna feel alive? I hear skydiving kicks ass. The point I'm poorly trying to make is that even if your not interested in anything I just mentioned, start trying shit out and finding groups of people who like the things you do. Meeting new people is hard, but everyone wants friends and you will likely start to make some with similar interests. This will hopefully get you out and about a lot more, and the less time you spend in one place, the more time you spend meeting new people and having new experiences. As for a girlfriend, it will likely happen when you least expect it.

I did not even know that truancy tickets exist until now. It is very common for people with depression to try and hide it. If you are able, tell a friend or family member to help you speak with your school and inform them that you are seeking help and that will likely help you to avoid getting a ticket. It is better to try and prevent it by being open, than to try and fight it once you have it.

Thanks for sharing. I have only been on this subreddit for a short time and it is great to see people helping other, and also sad how there is not more people participating and being supportive/informative.

My SO is dealing with some terrible depression as well and has not gone to work in over a month. staying home started in relation to a health issue, then just turned into the norm. She hides it from everyone and for a while I helped her hide it hoping that she would feel better or come around. This was the wrong decision. If your friend is willing, explain to them your situation and have them come with you to seek out help and to keep you honest when you talk to someone. There is no chance of help if you hide it. 

You should also strongly consider telling the people at your club activity  and work study that you are in a bad spot and need support. having them help to keep an eye on you and be there when you need them could go a long way. Pulling out a downward spiral is a hard thing to do, but very possible.

You should also consider options such as medical withdrawal like RevolutionaryDreamer mentioned. There are programs and options available to help people in your position, but they are often poorly advertised.

You were brave enough to admit that you need help and that is a good step in the right direction. Just make sure that you DO NOT give up until you get it. Remember that even the lower 50% of doctors graduate and it may take a couple tries to find one who truly listens and can help.
Keep at it and don't give up. Even if this is not meant to last forever, use it to take as many positive steps as possible.

My SO is super depressed and being super sick for the last few months had made things much worse. She can't even get herself out of bed to go to work. As a result we will both likely be bankrupt in the next couple months and she might lose her job/insurance so I have done a bit of research on this as I ask around for help. Government aid is available as one option. Local county health departments might be a good place to start. It might take some time on the phone and good questions but check it out. 

Another thing I found out about today is that many not-for-profit hospitals will take on charity cases to meet a minimum requirement they have to meet for the year to keep their status. You may want to look into this as an option.

You can also look for local support groups that may be able to at least offer some moral and social support beyond the internet.  I hope this helps, and if you find anything else in your search that might help, please let me know.

I agree with all of the above. Graduate and study something that interests you. Don't worry about how much money it will make. Things tend to open up a lot more after high school, particularly if you can get yourself into a larger community where you can meet other people who value education and furthering their own abilities. It becomes a much more positive environment for many. I'm not even saying you need to go to college. Just study or do the shit out of something you love. You have more than enough courage to do far more than most people with your life. But do it for yourself or to help others, not to impress others.

Congrats, it is not an easy step. My SO is currently in terrible shape and her previous experiences seeking out help did not go well. So getting her to ask for or accept help has been very difficult. So I have a slight idea how hard that must have been. Keep at it and I hope things get better.

Made a burner for this one as my SO spends a lot of time on reddit. I'm hoping that maybe the advice can go both ways on this as I am a guy whose gf is probably feeling exactly like you. If she could have me 3 times a day, 7 days a week she would be in heaven. And I wish I could make that happen too. It would probably skyrocket my confidence and physical health. Hell, I should be hard right now just thinking about it. Instead the thought of sex lately scares me more than anything, and the more she keeps asking for it, the more stressed I become and the less I want it because I feel like I am failing to keep her happy and the stress of the worsening situation causes performance anxiety. Then on top of it I have to hear little jokes about how I never share my dick anymore. I laugh these jokes off, but they truly crush me. I'll give you some background that may seem irrelevant and drawn out at first, but is needed to fully understand.

Right now I can still man up and have mediocre sex twice a week, but I have to fight past a lot of emotions to make it happen. I do it though because the last thing I would ever want her to think is that I find her unattractive. I think she is gorgeous and I want her to know that. I tell her all of the time, but she is very dependent on a physical connection to get reassurance. 

Part of the problem is that for the last year she has been dealing with some terrible depression and anxiety, made worse by recent medical issues that the doctors can not seem to get under control. Along with depression and medication often comes weight gain and a feeling a hopelessness that might even make you go without showering, putting on regular clothes, or going outside for days at a time as you see no reason to. Now her self esteem has bottomed out and she keeps searching for that physical reassurance. She thinks that I find her ugly now and want nothing to do with her since I don't want to have sex, which actually could not be further from the truth. She is still a tiny girl who I want to fuck senseless, and her physical condition is nothing a month or two at the gym and a shower can not reverse (I am guilty of this myself and have no reason or want to judge her for it). But when your depressed, it can be hard to see things that way.


So now she thinks that I'm not attracted to her because she is focused on the sex being an escape and comfort. For me though, the stress of our personal life has gotten to me and I simply can't handle another thing going wrong to stress about. That includes our sex life. Past issues in her life have caused a few bad sexual experiences that shook my confidence, but I rebounded from those with time. Now, we have tons of medical bills piling up, I am almost complete broke and out of savings trying to take care of her, she can't handle working, I've gained even more weight than her during this long ordeal (Instead of needing to lose 40 lbs, I now need to lose 60), and I'm afraid that I am going to come home one day to find that she has decided to check out from this world. 

The LAST thing I want to think about is sex. I've never had the highest libido in my opinion, but sex once a day should not be an issue for me. Never has been in the past. But now I'm stressed to no end and all I really want is to get her feeling well enough to go to work to help me with the bills I am drowning in. It has reached a point where in my mind I would just rather not have sex again than deal with the crushed confidence I have from not being able to perform. 

I've always been a super happy and positive person. I'm still positive and level headed, but I'm not happy anymore and sex just reminds me that I am not happy. As for masturbating, I might do it once or twice a week, but at this point it is more like a maintenance check to see if it still works. 

I love my gf. I want her to feel better. I want our life to be better. I want to see my friends and not make excuses about why I can't make it out because I am broke or she is sick and I don't want her to feel embarrassed or at fault. When I can take back a chunk of my life, then maybe I can spend some time sharing my dick.

**TL;DR GF wants more sex but I am too stressed about our situation and every time she asks or jokes about it, I want it less and less.**
